To prepare sugar water, dissolve 4 level teaspoons (20 g) of sugar in 200 ml of clean water. 4. A 50% glucose solution is equivalent to a 50% dextrose solution or D50, but note that this solution can irritate veins. Emergency Treatments for Malaria in Pregnancy 5. Urgently refer the pregnant woman with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria to a hospital. 6. After emergency management, discuss the treatment plan with the woman and her family. 7. Quickly arrange transportation and financial assistance if needed. 8. Inform the referral center in advance via radio or phone if possible. 9. Accompany the woman to the hospital if feasible, or send: A health worker trained in delivery care. A relative who can donate blood. The baby with the mother, if possible. Essential emergency drugs and supplies. Emergency Supplies for Transport and Home Delivery 10. Ensure the following supplies are available: IV catheters and tubing (2 sets). Gloves (at least 2 pairs, one sterile). Sterile syringes and needles (5 sets). Urinary catheter (1). Antiseptic solution (1 small bottle). Container for sharps (1). Trash bag (1). Torch and extra batteries (1). 11. If delivery is anticipated during transport, include: Soap and towels (2 sets). Disposable delivery kits (2 sets). Clean cloths for receiving, drying, and wrapping the baby (3). Clean clothes for the baby (1 set). Plastic bag for the placenta (1 set). Resuscitation bag and mask for the baby (1 set). Airway, Breathing, and Circulation Management 12. If the woman has severe difficulty breathing: Suspect airway obstruction and attempt to clear it. Help her find the best position for breathing. Urgently refer her to a hospital. 13. If the woman is unconscious: Position her on her back with arms at her sides. Tilt her head backward (unless trauma is suspected) and lift her chin to open the airway. Inspect her mouth for foreign objects and remove them if present. Clear secretions from her throat. IV Line and Fluid Administration 14. Wash hands with soap and water, and wear gloves. 15. Clean the IV insertion site with alcohol. 16. Insert an IV line using a 16-18 gauge needle and attach Ringer’s lactate or normal saline. 17. If the woman is in shock (systolic BP < 90 mmHg, pulse > 110/min, or heavy vaginal bleeding): Infuse 1 liter of fluid in 15-20 minutes as rapidly as possible. Infuse another liter in 30 minutes at 30 ml/min if needed. Monitor blood pressure, pulse, and signs of fluid overload every 15 minutes. 18. Adjust the infusion rate to 3 ml/min (1 liter over 6-8 hours) when the pulse slows to < 100/min and systolic BP rises to ≥ 100 mmHg. 19. If severe abdominal pain, obstructed labor, ectopic pregnancy, fever, or dehydration is present, infuse 1 liter over 2-3 hours. 20. For severe anemia or pre-eclampsia/eclampsia, infuse 1 liter over 6-8 hours. 21. If IV access is not possible, administer oral rehydration solution (ORS) by mouth or nasogastric tube (300-500 ml in 1 hour). Do not give ORS to unconscious women or those with convulsions. Management of Postpartum Hemorrhage 22. If heavy postpartum bleeding persists after placenta delivery or if the uterus is soft: Place a cupped palm on the uterine fundus to assess contraction. Massage the fundus in a circular motion until it contracts. Expel clots by applying downward pressure with fingers behind the fundus. Collect and measure blood loss. 23. If bleeding continues despite uterine massage and oxytocin/ergometrine treatment: Apply bimanual uterine compression. If bleeding persists, apply aortic compression and transport the woman to a hospital. Oxytocin Administration 24. For heavy postpartum bleeding: Administer 10 IU oxytocin IM/IV. Repeat 10 IU after 20 minutes if bleeding persists. For IV infusion, mix 20 IU in 1 liter of fluid at 60 drops/min. Do not exceed 3 liters of IV fluids containing oxytocin. Misoprostol Administration 25. If IV oxytocin is unavailable or ineffective, administer 800 µg misoprostol (4 tablets) sublingually. Ergometrine Administration 26. For heavy bleeding in early pregnancy or postpartum (after oxytocin), administer ergometrine unless contraindicated (e.g., eclampsia, pre-eclampsia, hypertension, or retained placenta). Manual Removal of Placenta 27. If the placenta is not delivered within 1 hour after birth or if heavy bleeding continues: Explain the procedure to the woman and obtain consent. Insert an IV line and administer fluids. Assist the woman onto her back and administer diazepam (10 mg IM/IV). Clean the vulva and perineal area, and ensure the bladder is empty. Insert a gloved hand into the uterus to detach and remove the placenta. Explore the uterine cavity to ensure all placental tissue is removed. 28. If the placenta does not separate easily, suspect placenta accreta and urgently refer to a hospital. Tear Repair and Bladder Management 29. Examine and classify the tear: For firstor second-degree tears, suture if heavy bleeding persists. For thirdor fourth-degree tears, cover with a clean pad and urgently refer to a hospital. 30. If the bladder is distended and the woman cannot urinate, encourage urination or catheterize the bladder. Eclampsia and Pre-Eclampsia Management 31. Administer magnesium sulfate for severe pre-eclampsia or eclampsia: IV: 4 g over 20 minutes. IM: 10 g (5 g in each buttock) with 1 ml of 2% lignocaine. 32. If convulsions recur, administer an additional 2 g magnesium sulfate IV over 20 minutes. 33. Monitor urine output, respiratory rate, and reflexes before administering the next dose. 34. If magnesium sulfate is unavailable or contraindicated, administer diazepam: IV: 10 mg slowly over 2 minutes. Rectally: 20 mg using a lubricated syringe. Important Considerations 35. Do not leave the woman unattended. Position her on her left side and protect her from injury. 36. Administer magnesium sulfate slowly to avoid respiratory depression. If respiratory depression occurs, administer calcium gluconate (1 g IV over 10 minutes). 37. Urgently refer the woman to a hospital unless delivery is imminent.
